findings.reason: a coordinator reading the followup chain dispatches §3 and closes the chain believing the plan has no other open section, leaving §65 undispatched and the false "only open section" claim in the record.
findings.text: §65 is declared `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations` (docs/plans/the-suite-is-green-at-head.html:27) and has a heading and body at :893, but the plan carries only one open followup, f-tsigah-066, which recommends §3 and whose body asserts "§3 … is the plan's only open section"; there is no `f-*` recommending `/reckon-build the-suite-is-green-at-head §65`, so the plan's own dispatch chain names one of its two open sections and misstates the count

findings.reason: the section's second branch must name the clock that actually feeds the age (`recovery_classification._utc_seconds`, from `recovery_watch`), or a node can satisfy the letter of the deliverable and still leave the assertion time-dependent.
findings.text: §65 allows the repair to be "the clock is frozen for the case", but `home` already freezes `obligations._utc_now` to `NOW` (tests/test_an_obligation_never_offers_a_promotion_past_a_blocking_finding.py:34) and the age still drifts: the missing-review duty's `age` comes from `row["terminal_age_seconds"]`, computed in `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:1320` from `moment`, which is `_utc_seconds()` (`recovery_classification.py:829`, defined at `reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:517`) because `recovery.classify_pointer(pointer)` is called with no `now_seconds` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:985`); freezing `obligations._utc_now` therefore leaves the real-clock read intact, and the file passes alone today, so a node taking that branch can close the section with the drift unchanged

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `tests/test_an_obligation_never_offers_a_promotion_past_a_blocking_finding.py` and the cited id exist, the file has exactly the 7 tests the section claims ("7 passed" reproduced here), "promotion-evidence §5" resolves to `a-promotion-reads-the-evidence-it-is-given.html` §5 whose done-when runs the importer population of `reckon.crew.review` (which this file imports), and the failing message format `{age // 60}m {age % 60}s` matches the quoted "51m 0s".
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §65's done-when is measurable (the cited id passes with the clock advanced two minutes and passes otherwise), and it declares a logged negative control (restore the import-time `NOW` with the clock advanced) that genuinely fails on the unfixed file: `NOW` is captured at import (tests/test_an_obligation_never_offers_a_promotion_past_a_blocking_finding.py:20) while the age is read from the real clock at assertion time, so a two-minute advance yields 52m and `assert "50m" in row["next_command"]` (line 179) fails.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section carries the plan's standing convention that every gate log opens with revision and literal command and ends in a bare `EXIT=` line; it names no directory, the same shape §64 was declined for, and the plan's sixty sibling sections state "logged under the run directory", so this is the house convention rather than a new gap.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no stage labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol or a source path; the section names its mechanism (an import-time clock in a test).
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence, but the section's second permitted repair ("the clock is frozen for the case") is already the file's state and cannot remove the drift, because the pinned clock and the clock the age reads are different ones.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §65 carries one deliverable (derive the file's ages from the clock the code under test reads, or freeze that clock) on one write path.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §65 was added as `implementable` but no followup recommends it, while f-tsigah-066's body states §3 is "the plan's only open section", which the plan's own declarations contradict.
